_: Hand-written prose for the roadmap's 'Known bugs' block. NOT a list of what is on the
page — the issue tracker is that, and this file cannot add or remove an entry.
A bug appears when its issue is open and carries BOTH `bug` and `accepted`, and
vanishes the moment it is closed. Applying a label needs Triage, so `accepted` is a
gate closed to the people who file and open to me. That matters: anyone can file, this
page is published, and escaping a stranger's text stops markup getting through without
making a wrong report right.
overrides — keyed by issue number as a string. A generated entry is a starting
point, not a verdict: whatever is here wins over what the reporter
wrote. The issue is the source of the FACT that the bug is open; this is
the source of how it reads.
title      replace the heading
railLabel  shorter label for the contents rail
html       replace the body outright, as lines of HTML
note       append one paragraph, keeping the reporter's prose
hide       true to keep the issue open but off the page
manual    — an escape hatch for a bug with no issue at all, and it should normally
stay EMPTY. Everything on the roadmap ought to trace back to an accepted
issue, so that closing that issue is all it takes to correct the page. An
entry here is a promise I have to remember to keep by hand.
Render with `node scripts/roadmap-data.mjs`.

14.title: Legacy catalogue exports can still re-import as books
html: 1.1.1 made the catalogue export always write type: movie /
type: show, which is what routes a file back to the right importer.
Files exported by 1.1.0 or earlier were not rewritten, so a bare
film export from then — no director, no collection, no character/actor/timestamp on
any line — still carries nothing identifying it. Re-export it, or add a
type: line by hand. Not fixable retroactively: a detector cannot infer
